source.text: Πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ χριστὸς ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ γεγέννηται, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὸν γεννήσαντα ἀγαπᾷ καὶ τὸν γεγεννημένον ἐξ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Everyone the believing that Jesus is the Christ from the God has been born, and everyone the loving the [one] having fathered loves also the [one] having been fathered from him.

en.L: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} has been born of God, and everyone who loves the one who fathered loves also the one fathered by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} has been born of God, and everyone who loves the Father loves the child born of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as well.
en.R: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} has been born as a child of God. And everyone who loves God the Father also loves {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children.

es.L: Todo el que cree que Jesús es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} ha nacido de Dios, y todo el que ama al que engendró ama también al engendrado por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Todo el que cree que Jesús es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} ha nacido de Dios, y todo el que ama al Padre ama también a quien ha nacido de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Todo el que cree que Jesús es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} ha nacido de Dios y es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} hijo. Y todo el que ama a Dios Padre ama también a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hijos.

fr.L: Quiconque croit que Jésus est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est né de Dieu, et quiconque aime celui qui a engendré aime aussi celui qui a été engendré par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Celui qui croit que Jésus est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est né de Dieu, et celui qui aime le Père aime aussi l’enfant qui est né de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Tous ceux qui croient que Jésus est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} sont nés de Dieu : ce sont {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} enfants. Et tous ceux qui aiment Dieu le Père aiment aussi {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} enfants.

sw.L: Kila anayeamini kwamba Yesu ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} amezaliwa kutoka kwa Mungu, na kila anayempenda aliyezaa anampenda pia aliyezaliwa kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: Kila anayeamini kwamba Yesu ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} amezaliwa na Mungu, na kila anayempenda Baba anampenda pia mtoto aliyezaliwa kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.R: Kila anayeamini kwamba Yesu ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} amezaliwa kuwa mtoto wa Mungu. Na kila anayempenda Mungu Baba anawapenda pia watoto {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

ko.L: 예수께서 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이심을 믿는 사람은 누구나 하나님에게서 났습니다. 그리고 낳으신 분을 사랑하는 사람은 누구나 그분에게서 난 이도 사랑합니다.
ko.B: 예수께서 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이심을 믿는 사람은 누구나 하나님에게서 태어났습니다. 그리고 아버지를 사랑하는 사람은 누구나 그분에게서 태어난 자녀도 사랑합니다.
ko.R: 예수께서 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이심을 믿는 사람은 누구나 하나님의 자녀로 태어났습니다. 그리고 하나님 아버지를 사랑하는 사람은 누구나 그분의 자녀들도 사랑합니다.

vi.L: Ai tin rằng Đức Giê-xu là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} thì đã được sinh ra từ Đức Chúa Trời, và ai yêu thương Đấng đã sinh thành thì cũng yêu thương người được {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sinh ra.
vi.B: Ai tin rằng Đức Giê-xu là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} thì đã được sinh ra từ Đức Chúa Trời, và ai yêu thương Cha thì cũng yêu thương người con được {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sinh ra.
vi.R: Ai tin rằng Đức Giê-xu là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} thì đã được sinh ra làm con cái Đức Chúa Trời. Và ai yêu thương Đức Chúa Trời là Cha thì cũng yêu thương con cái {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: believing that Jesus is the Christ goes together with having been born of God
alternatives: the new birth comes first and produces belief
decisions.reason: The verb for being born (γεγέννηται) is perfect: the birth is a settled fact, while the believing is present and ongoing. The sentence says that everyone who believes is born of God; it does not spell out which comes first. The same pairing of a present action with the perfect "has been born" is used of doing right (2:29) and loving (4:7).

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, God's anointed king
decisions.reason: With the article, ὁ χριστὸς is a title, as in 2:22: the confession is that the man Jesus is the promised Messiah. The christos setting gives "Christ" or "Messiah".

decisions.choice: a rule from family life applied to God and his children: whoever loves the parent loves the parent's child
alternatives: the one born of him is Jesus, the Son
a general proverb with no particular parent in view
decisions.reason: The one who fathered is God, named in the first half of the verse. The one born of him is any believer: the next verse speaks of "the children of God", and the first half of this verse has just said believers are born of God. The singular states a general rule that holds for each child. The other reading, that the child is Jesus, is possible, but the letter does not use this verb of the Son until 5:18.

decisions.choice: the Father
decisions.reason: The participle names God by what he did: he fathered the children. Balanced says "the Father", which is what the participle means here; Literal keeps the participle.

decisions.choice: has been born as a child of God; God the Father ... his children
alternatives: has been born of God; the one who fathered ... the one born of him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the birth makes a person (a child of God) and names God as the Father. It puts the rule in the plural, "his children", because the singular child stands for every believer (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: al que engendró ... al engendrado por él (L); al Padre ... a quien ha nacido de él (B)
decisions.reason: "Engendrar" is the plain Spanish verb for a father begetting a child, as in Hebrews 1:5, and Literal keeps the family rule of meaning decision m3 in its own words. Balanced names the Father and says "ha nacido de él", as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}
decisions.reason: Here "Christ" is a title with the article (m2), so the article stays outside the span and both readings are natural: "el Cristo", "el Mesías". The same wherever 1 John says that Jesus is the Christ.

decisions.choice: quiconque (L); celui qui (B); tous ceux qui (R)
decisions.reason: "Tout homme qui" would need the gender setting, and "toute personne qui" would make the agreeing words feminine ("née"). "Quiconque" and "celui qui" are generic in French and agree in the masculine, so no setting is needed; Readable puts the rule in the plural, as the English Readable does with "children".

decisions.choice: amezaliwa kutoka kwa Mungu (L); amezaliwa na Mungu (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "from" with "kutoka kwa". Balanced and Readable use the passive with "na", the ordinary Swahili way of naming who gave birth, so "born of God" reads as God's own act. "Kuzaa" is used of either parent, so Literal can say "aliyezaa" for the one who fathered.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: As in Galatians and Jude: Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb ("anayempenda", loves him), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives ("kwake", "wake", "zake"), and Swahili has fewer spans than English in this letter.

decisions.choice: "낳으신 분 ... 그분에게서 난 이" (L); "아버지 ... 태어난 자녀" (B)
decisions.reason: The verse applies a rule from family life to God and his children (meaning decision): whoever loves the parent loves the parent's child. Literal keeps the Greek's two forms of one verb, "fathered" and "fathered by him", with "낳다"; Balanced names Father and child, as the English does.

source.text: ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἀγαπῶμεν τὰ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅταν τὸν θεὸν ἀγαπῶμεν καὶ τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ ποιῶμεν·

records.literal_gloss: In this we know that we love the children of the God, whenever the God we love and the commandments of him we do;

en.L: In this we know that we love the children of God: whenever we love God and do {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments;
en.B: We can tell that we love God's children when we love God and do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commands.
en.R: We know that we love God's children when we love God and obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands.

es.L: En esto sabemos que amamos a los hijos de Dios: cuando amamos a Dios y cumplimos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos.
es.B: Sabemos que amamos a los hijos de Dios cuando amamos a Dios y hacemos lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} manda.
es.R: Sabemos que amamos a los hijos de Dios cuando amamos a Dios y obedecemos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandatos.

fr.L: En ceci nous savons que nous aimons les enfants de Dieu : lorsque nous aimons Dieu et que nous faisons {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements ;
fr.B: Nous pouvons savoir que nous aimons les enfants de Dieu quand nous aimons Dieu et que nous faisons ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commande.
fr.R: Nous savons que nous aimons les enfants de Dieu quand nous aimons Dieu et que nous obéissons à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements.

sw.L: Katika hili tunajua kwamba tunawapenda watoto wa Mungu: tunapompenda Mungu na kuzitenda amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.B: Tunajua kwamba tunawapenda watoto wa Mungu tunapompenda Mungu na kufanya yale anayoagiza.
sw.R: Tunajua kwamba tunawapenda watoto wa Mungu tunapompenda Mungu na kutii amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.

ko.L: 우리가 하나님을 사랑하고 그분의 계명들을 행할 때마다, 이것으로 우리가 하나님의 자녀들을 사랑한다는 것을 압니다.
ko.B: 우리가 하나님을 사랑하고 그분이 명령하신 것을 행할 때, 우리는 우리가 하나님의 자녀들을 사랑한다는 것을 압니다.
ko.R: 우리가 하나님을 사랑하고 그분의 계명에 순종할 때, 우리는 우리가 하나님의 자녀들을 사랑한다는 것을 압니다.

vi.L: Bởi điều này chúng ta biết rằng chúng ta yêu thương con cái Đức Chúa Trời: khi chúng ta yêu thương Đức Chúa Trời và làm theo các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}};
vi.B: Chúng ta có thể biết mình yêu thương con cái Đức Chúa Trời khi chúng ta yêu thương Đức Chúa Trời và làm theo điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} truyền dạy.
vi.R: Chúng ta biết rằng mình yêu thương con cái Đức Chúa Trời khi chúng ta yêu thương Đức Chúa Trời và vâng giữ các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: "in this" points forward to the "whenever" clause
decisions.reason: In 1 John ἐν τούτῳ can point either way; here the clause with ὅταν (whenever) supplies what "this" is.

decisions.choice: love for God and love for God's children cannot be separated, and each is a test of the other
alternatives: love for God depends on loving others first
decisions.reason: In 4:20 love for the brother or sister is the test of love for God; here love for God and obedience to him are the test of love for his children. The two verses look at the same bond from opposite sides; neither kind of love can exist without the other.

decisions.choice: God's children, of either sex
decisions.reason: τέκνα is neuter and already inclusive, so the gender setting does not apply.

decisions.choice: "do" his commandments (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have "keep", the verb John uses for commandments elsewhere in the letter and in the next verse; the SBLGNT follows manuscripts that read "do", the less usual expression. The meaning is the same, so no footnote. A reviewer should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: do what he commands (B); obey his commands (R)
decisions.reason: "Do commandments" is not natural English; the sense is carrying them out. Literal keeps "do", the Greek verb.

decisions.choice: los hijos de Dios, no gender span
alternatives: los hijos y las hijas de Dios
decisions.reason: The plural "hijos" already includes daughters (m3), as "hermanos" includes sisters, so it takes no gender span.

source.text: αὕτη γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ ἵνα τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ τηρῶμεν, καὶ αἱ ἐντολαὶ αὐτοῦ βαρεῖαι οὐκ εἰσίν, ὅτι πᾶν τὸ γεγεννημένον ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ νικᾷ τὸν κόσμον.

records.literal_gloss: This for is the love of the God, that the commandments of him we keep, and the commandments of him heavy not are, \v 4 because everything the having been born from the God overcomes the world.

en.L: For this is the love of God, that we keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments; and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments are not heavy, \v 4 because everything that has been born of God overcomes the world.
en.B: For to love God is to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments are no burden, \v 4 because everything born of God overcomes the world.
en.R: Loving God means obeying {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands. And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands are not too hard for us, \v 4 because every child of God overcomes the world.

es.L: Porque el amor de Dios es este: que guardemos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos; y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos no son pesados, \v 4 porque todo lo nacido de Dios vence al mundo.
es.B: Porque amar a Dios es guardar {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandamientos no son una carga, \v 4 porque todo lo que ha nacido de Dios vence al mundo.
es.R: Amar a Dios significa obedecer {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandatos. Y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} mandatos no son demasiado difíciles para nosotros, \v 4 porque todo hijo de Dios vence al mundo.

fr.L: Car ceci est l’amour de Dieu : que nous gardions {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements ; et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements ne sont pas lourds, \v 4 parce que tout ce qui est né de Dieu vainc le monde.
fr.B: Car aimer Dieu, c’est garder {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements ne sont pas un fardeau, \v 4 parce que tout ce qui est né de Dieu est vainqueur du monde.
fr.R: Aimer Dieu, c’est obéir à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements. Et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} commandements ne sont pas trop difficiles pour nous, \v 4 parce que tout enfant de Dieu remporte la victoire sur le monde.

sw.L: Kwa maana upendo wa Mungu ni huu, kwamba tushike amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}; na amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} hazina uzito, \v 4 kwa sababu kila kilichozaliwa kutoka kwa Mungu kinaushinda ulimwengu.
sw.B: Kwa maana kumpenda Mungu ni kushika amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, na amri hizo si mzigo, \v 4 kwa sababu kila kilichozaliwa na Mungu kinaushinda ulimwengu.
sw.R: Kumpenda Mungu maana yake ni kutii amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Na amri {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} si ngumu mno kwetu, \v 4 kwa sababu kila mtoto wa Mungu anaushinda ulimwengu.

ko.L: 하나님을 사랑하는 것은 이것이니, 곧 우리가 그분의 계명들을 지키는 것입니다. 그리고 그분의 계명들은 무겁지 않습니다. \v 4 하나님에게서 난 모든 것은 세상을 이기기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 하나님을 사랑한다는 것은 그분의 계명을 지키는 것입니다. 그리고 그분의 계명은 무거운 짐이 아닙니다. \v 4 하나님에게서 태어난 모든 사람은 세상을 이기기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 하나님을 사랑한다는 것은 그분의 계명에 순종한다는 뜻입니다. 그리고 그분의 계명은 우리에게 너무 어렵지 않습니다. \v 4 하나님의 자녀는 누구나 세상을 이기기 때문입니다.

vi.L: Vì đây là tình yêu thương đối với Đức Chúa Trời: chúng ta giữ các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; và các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không nặng nề, \v 4 vì mọi điều được sinh ra từ Đức Chúa Trời thì thắng thế gian.
vi.B: Vì yêu thương Đức Chúa Trời là giữ các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không phải là gánh nặng, \v 4 vì mọi điều được sinh ra từ Đức Chúa Trời đều thắng thế gian.
vi.R: Yêu thương Đức Chúa Trời nghĩa là vâng giữ các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Và các điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không quá khó cho chúng ta, \v 4 vì mọi người con của Đức Chúa Trời đều thắng thế gian.

decisions.choice: love for God
decisions.reason: The genitive could name God as the one who loves or as the one loved. Verse 2 has just spoken of loving God, and the love is shown in keeping his commandments, so it is our love for him.

decisions.choice: not burdensome, not a crushing weight
decisions.reason: βαρεῖαι means heavy, and so oppressive (compare the heavy burdens of Matthew 23:4). The point is not that obeying costs nothing but that the commandments do not crush the one who is born of God, because that person has the strength to overcome. Compare Deuteronomy 30:11, where God's commandment is not too hard or far away.

decisions.choice: everything born of God: every person born of God, put as a whole
alternatives: only certain things given by God
decisions.reason: The neuter πᾶν τὸ γεγεννημένον speaks of all who are born of God as one whole (compare John 6:37, 39, where the neuter "all that" also stands for people). It means believers, as 5:1 and 5:4b show.

decisions.choice: the world: human life organized apart from God and against him
decisions.reason: Key term. As in 2:15-17 and 4:4-5, the world is the realm that does not know God and is under the evil one (5:19). To overcome it is to stand firm against it, as Jesus overcame the world (John 16:33).

decisions.choice: to love God is to keep his commandments
alternatives: this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments
decisions.reason: Balanced states the equation plainly, using the sense in meaning decision m1; "the love of God" could be read as God's love for us.

decisions.choice: every child of God
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant (meaning decision m3) in the wording 5:1 uses.

decisions.choice: todo lo nacido de Dios (L); todo lo que ha nacido de Dios (B)
alternatives: todo el que ha nacido de Dios
decisions.reason: The Greek is neuter, every person born of God put as a whole (m3), and Spanish can keep that with the neuter "lo". Readable says "todo hijo de Dios", as the English Readable says "every child of God".

decisions.choice: vaincre (L), être vainqueur (B), remporter la victoire (R); the same in 5:4b and 5:5
decisions.reason: "Vaincre" keeps the link between the verb and the noun "la victoire" in 5:4b, as the Greek does. Its present forms ("vainc") are rare, so Balanced says "est vainqueur" and Readable "remporte la victoire", the plain words the English Readable also uses.

decisions.choice: kushika amri (L, B), kutii amri (R); kushinda ulimwengu
decisions.reason: As in John 14:15: "kushika" (keep) for keeping commandments, and Readable says "kutii" (obey), as the English Readable says "obey". "Ulimwengu" is the world as John uses it (m4), and "kushinda" (overcome) is the same verb in verses 4 and 5.

decisions.choice: kila kilichozaliwa
decisions.reason: The Greek is neuter, every person born of God put as a whole (m3). The class 7 form "kilichozaliwa" keeps that, as the English keeps "everything"; Readable says "kila mtoto wa Mungu".

decisions.choice: "하나님을 사랑하는 것" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the phrase here as love for God, so Korean says so plainly at every level; the open genitive would be read as God's love.

decisions.choice: "하나님에게서 난 모든 것" (L); "모든 사람" (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses a neuter, "everything born of God", for every person born of God put as a whole (meaning decision). Literal keeps "것"; Balanced and Readable say "사람" and "자녀".

decisions.choice: "tình yêu thương đối với Đức Chúa Trời" (L) for "the love of God"
alternatives: "tình yêu thương của Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: Here the love of God is love for God (m1). "Của Đức Chúa Trời" would be read as God's own love, so Literal says "đối với".

decisions.choice: "mọi điều được sinh ra" (L, B) for "everything born of God"
decisions.reason: The Greek puts it as a whole, "everything", though people are meant (m3). Literal and Balanced keep the general word, as the English does; Readable says every child of God.

source.text: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ νίκη ἡ νικήσασα τὸν κόσμον, ἡ πίστις ἡμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: And this is the victory the having overcome the world, the faith of us;

en.L: And this is the victory that overcame the world: our faith;
en.B: And our faith is the victory that overcame the world.
en.R: Our faith is how we have won the victory over the world.

es.L: Y esta es la victoria que venció al mundo: nuestra fe.
es.B: Y nuestra fe es la victoria que venció al mundo.
es.R: Nuestra fe es la manera en que ya hemos vencido al mundo.

fr.L: Et ceci est la victoire qui a vaincu le monde : notre foi ;
fr.B: Et notre foi est la victoire qui a vaincu le monde.
fr.R: C’est par notre foi que nous avons remporté la victoire sur le monde.

decisions.choice: the victory that overcame: a victory already won
alternatives: a victory that keeps on being won
decisions.reason: The participle νικήσασα is aorist, unlike the present "overcomes" just before. It looks back to a victory already won: the moment believers came to faith, which shares in Jesus' own victory (John 16:33 "I have overcome the world"; compare 1 John 2:13-14; 4:4).

decisions.choice: our faith: our believing that Jesus is the Son of God
decisions.reason: Key term. This is the only place the noun πίστις occurs in John's letters, and John's Gospel never uses it; elsewhere John always uses the verb "believe". The next verse defines it: believing that Jesus is the Son of God.

decisions.choice: our faith first
alternatives: this is the victory that overcame the world: our faith
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "our faith" last for emphasis. Balanced and Readable make it the subject, which keeps the weight on it without the delayed construction.

decisions.choice: how we have won the victory over the world
alternatives: the victory that overcame the world
decisions.reason: Readable says what the faith does in plain words; the other levels keep "overcame" so the verb links to verses 4a and 5.

decisions.choice: "믿음" for faith, the noun, at every level
decisions.reason: The only place the noun "faith" occurs in John's letters; Korean gives it the key-term word of the other books, "믿음", which also links it with the verb "믿다" in verses 1, 5 and 10.

decisions.choice: "đức tin" for faith
decisions.reason: The letter uses the noun only here; it is our believing that Jesus is the Son of God (m2). Vietnamese keeps "đức tin", the key term for faith in the Vietnamese Romans and James, beside the verb "tin" of 5:1 and 5:5.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer: only the believer
decisions.reason: The question with "if not" is a strong way of saying that the believer, and no one else, overcomes the world. It names the faith of 5:4b: believing that Jesus is the Son of God.

decisions.choice: Jesus himself is the Son of God
alternatives: the Son of God is a being distinct from the man Jesus
decisions.reason: The confession is that the man Jesus is the Son of God, not merely that a heavenly Son exists. 4:2-3 and 5:6 press the same point against those who left the community (2:19).

decisions.choice: a question and a separate answer
decisions.reason: Readable turns the rhetorical question into a question and its answer, which is what the Greek means (meaning decision m1).

sw.L: Huyu ni yule aliyekuja kupitia maji na damu, Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}; si katika maji peke yake, bali katika maji na katika damu; na anayeshuhudia ni Roho, kwa kuwa Roho ni kweli.

sw.R: Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ndiye aliyekuja kupitia maji na damu. Hakuja na maji peke yake. Alikuja na maji na damu. Na Roho ni shahidi wa jambo hili, kwa sababu Roho ni kweli.

ko.L: 이분이 물과 피로 오신 분, 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이십니다. 물로만이 아니라 물과 피로 [오셨습니다]. 그리고 증언하시는 분은 성령이십니다. 성령은 진리이시기 때문입니다.

ko.R: 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 물과 피를 통해 오신 분이십니다. 그분은 물로만 오신 것이 아닙니다. 물과 피로 오셨습니다. 그리고 성령께서 이것을 증언하십니다. 성령은 진리이시기 때문입니다.

vi.L: Đây là Đấng đã đến bởi nước và huyết, là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}; không phải chỉ trong nước mà thôi, nhưng trong nước và trong huyết; và Thánh Linh là Đấng làm chứng, vì Thánh Linh là chân lý.
vi.B: Đây là Đấng đã đến bởi nước và huyết: Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. Ngài đã đến không phải chỉ với nước mà thôi, nhưng với nước và với huyết. Và chính Thánh Linh là Đấng làm chứng, vì Thánh Linh là chân lý.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} là Đấng đã đến qua nước và huyết. Ngài không đến chỉ với nước mà thôi. Ngài đã đến với nước và với huyết. Và Thánh Linh làm chứng về điều này, vì Thánh Linh là chân lý.

decisions.choice: water and blood: most likely Jesus' baptism and his death on the cross
alternatives: the water and blood that flowed from Jesus' side when he died (John 19:34)
the sacraments of baptism and the Lord's Supper
decisions.reason: "Came" is aorist and looks at Jesus' coming in the past, so water and blood are events in his life. The most likely reading is his baptism, where the Spirit came on him and he was made known (John 1:31-34), and his death, where his blood was shed (1:7). "Not in the water only" seems aimed at teachers who accepted the baptism but denied that the Christ died; the letter insists that Jesus Christ came in the flesh (4:2). The other side: John 19:34-35 also joins water, blood and witness at the cross, and the writer may have that moment in mind. The text does not say which events it means, so a footnote gives the other readings.

decisions.choice: through ... in: two ways of saying the same coming
alternatives: a different meaning for each preposition
decisions.reason: The first phrase uses δι (through), the second ἐν (in, with). Both describe the means and circumstances of his coming; the change does not mark a different idea.

decisions.choice: because the Spirit is the truth
alternatives: that the Spirit is the truth (what the Spirit testifies)
decisions.reason: ὅτι could give the reason (because) or the content (testifies that). The Spirit's witness is trustworthy because the Spirit is the truth itself (John 14:17; 15:26, "the Spirit of truth"); the content of his testimony is about the Son (5:9-11), not about himself.

decisions.choice: water and blood (SBLGNT)
alternatives: water and blood and Spirit (some manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "and Spirit" or "and Holy Spirit" after "blood", or replace "blood" with "Spirit", probably under the influence of John 3:5 and of verse 8. The SBLGNT follows manuscripts with the shorter text. A reviewer should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: with the water ... with the blood
alternatives: in the water ... in the blood
decisions.reason: English "in the water" suggests standing in water. "With" carries the sense of meaning decision m2; Literal keeps "in".

decisions.choice: is a witness to this
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer "witness" and says what the Spirit testifies to: Jesus' coming just described.

decisions.choice: dar testimonio, testimonio (L, B); es testigo (R)
decisions.reason: Verses 6-11 turn on one verb and its noun. "Dar testimonio" and "testimonio" keep them visibly the same word in Spanish, as John's Gospel does. Readable says "es testigo", as the English Readable says "is a witness".

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: As in Galatians and Jude, the default is the usual Spanish name "Jesucristo", and the alternative separates name and title. Where a comma must follow the alternative, it sits inside the span.

decisions.choice: rendre témoignage, le témoignage (L, B); être le témoin (R); the same through 5:11
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for this verb family is kept at Literal and Balanced, so the testimony of verses 6-11 reads as one chain. Readable says "témoin", as the English Readable says "witness", and "dire" where the English Readable says "tell" (5:9-10).

decisions.choice: kushuhudia, ushuhuda (L, B); shahidi (R)
decisions.reason: As in John's Gospel: verses 6-11 turn on one verb and its noun, and "kushuhudia" and "ushuhuda" keep them visibly the same word. Readable says "shahidi" (a witness), as the English Readable does. "Kweli" for truth, as in John.

decisions.choice: "물과 피" at every level; "증언하시는 분 ... 성령" with the honorific
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads water and blood as most likely Jesus's baptism and death, and footnotes the other readings. Korean keeps the words, as the English does, so the reading stays with the meaning decision. The Spirit takes the honorific as a person who testifies.

decisions.choice: "huyết" for blood at every level here (5:6-8)
decisions.reason: The blood is most likely Jesus' death on the cross (m1, uncertain). The Vietnamese Colossians uses "huyết" for the blood of Christ and "máu" at Readable (1:20); here the three witnesses must keep one name each, so Readable keeps "huyết" too.

source.text: ὅτι τρεῖς εἰσιν οἱ μαρτυροῦντες, τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ τὸ ὕδωρ καὶ τὸ αἷμα, καὶ οἱ τρεῖς εἰς τὸ ἕν εἰσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Because three are the [ones] testifying, \v 8 the Spirit and the water and the blood, and the three into the one are.

en.L: For there are three who testify, \v 8 the Spirit and the water and the blood, and the three are for the one [thing].
en.B: For there are three that testify: \v 8 the Spirit, the water and the blood, and the three are in agreement.
en.R: So there are three witnesses: \v 8 the Spirit, the water and the blood. And all three say the same thing.

es.L: Porque tres son los que dan testimonio, \v 8 el Espíritu y el agua y la sangre, y los tres son para una [sola cosa].
es.B: Porque hay tres que dan testimonio: \v 8 el Espíritu, el agua y la sangre, y los tres están de acuerdo.
