fr.L: Car il y en a trois qui rendent témoignage, \v 8 l’Esprit et l’eau et le sang, et les trois sont pour l’unique [chose].
fr.B: Car il y en a trois qui rendent témoignage : \v 8 l’Esprit, l’eau et le sang, et les trois sont d’accord.
fr.R: Il y a donc trois témoins : \v 8 l’Esprit, l’eau et le sang. Et tous les trois disent la même chose.

sw.L: Kwa sababu wapo watatu wanaoshuhudia, \v 8 Roho na maji na damu, na hao watatu ni kwa [jambo] moja.
sw.B: Kwa maana wapo watatu wanaoshuhudia: \v 8 Roho, maji na damu, na hao watatu wanakubaliana.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo wapo mashahidi watatu: \v 8 Roho, maji na damu. Na wote watatu wanasema jambo lilelile.

ko.L: 증언하는 이가 셋이기 때문입니다. \v 8 성령과 물과 피입니다. 그리고 이 셋은 하나로 일치합니다.
ko.B: 증언하는 것이 셋 있습니다. \v 8 성령과 물과 피입니다. 그리고 이 셋은 서로 일치합니다.
ko.R: 그래서 증인이 셋 있습니다. \v 8 성령과 물과 피입니다. 그리고 이 셋은 모두 같은 것을 말합니다.

vi.L: Vì có ba [đấng] làm chứng, \v 8 là Thánh Linh, nước và huyết, và ba [đấng] ấy hiệp về một.
vi.B: Vì có ba điều làm chứng: \v 8 Thánh Linh, nước và huyết, và cả ba đều đồng nhất với nhau.
vi.R: Vậy có ba nhân chứng: \v 8 Thánh Linh, nước và huyết. Và cả ba đều nói cùng một điều.

decisions.choice: the short text, as in the SBLGNT: three that testify, the Spirit, the water and the blood
alternatives: the long text known as the Johannine Comma, which adds in verse 7 "in heaven, the Father, the Word and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one" and in verse 8 "there are three that testify on earth"
decisions.reason: The longer wording is not found in any Greek manuscript before the late medieval period; it appears in only a handful of late Greek manuscripts, some of them with the words added in the margin by a later hand. No Greek writer of the early church quotes it, even in the fourth-century debates about the Trinity, where it would have been the most useful verse to cite. It first appears in Latin writers and then in later copies of the Latin Bible, and it is missing from the oldest Latin Bible manuscripts and from the early translations into other languages. It probably began as a comment explaining the three witnesses, which was later copied into the text. From the Latin tradition it entered the printed Greek New Testament in the sixteenth century, and so the Textus Receptus and the King James Version (1611). The SBLGNT does not print it, and no level of this translation includes it. The doctrine of the Trinity does not rest on this passage. A reviewer must check this account against the SBLGNT apparatus and the manuscript evidence before the sentence is marked meaning reviewed.

decisions.choice: for: it explains the Spirit's testimony in verse 6
decisions.reason: ὅτι links the verse to the end of verse 6: the Spirit testifies, and it does not testify alone. Under the law of Moses a matter is settled by two or three witnesses (Deuteronomy 19:15; compare John 8:17).

decisions.choice: the three agree: they point to one and the same truth
decisions.reason: εἰς τὸ ἕν εἰσιν means literally "are into the one", that is, they converge on one thing: the single testimony about the Son (5:9-11). It says they agree, not that they are the same.

decisions.choice: the Spirit, the water and the blood: the Spirit's present witness together with the events of Jesus' baptism and death
alternatives: three sacraments or rites in the church's life
decisions.reason: The water and the blood are those of verse 6. The verbs are now present ("there are three that testify"): what happened at Jesus' baptism and death still bears witness, together with the Spirit. Some see a reference to baptism and the Lord's Supper in the church; the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: all three say the same thing
decisions.reason: Readable puts the idiom (meaning decision m3) in everyday words.

decisions.choice: So
decisions.reason: Readable uses "So" to start a fresh sentence that still follows on from verse 6; "For" at the start of a sentence is formal.

decisions.choice: "증언하는 이가 셋" (L); "증언하는 것이 셋" (B); "증인이 셋" (R)
alternatives: "하늘에서 증언하는 이가 셋이니 아버지와 말씀과 성령이라"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision follows the short text of the SBLGNT and footnotes the longer wording that appears in late manuscripts and in older Korean Bibles. Korean "이" (L) and "것" (B) let the Spirit and the things stand together as the Greek's masculine does; Readable says "witnesses".

decisions.choice: "ba [đấng]" (L), "ba điều" (B), "ba nhân chứng" (R) for the three who testify
decisions.reason: The Greek "three" is masculine, as if of persons, though two of the three are water and blood. Literal brackets a person word, lowercase; Balanced says "things"; Readable calls them witnesses, as the English does. The short text of the SBLGNT is followed (m1).

source.text: εἰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν τῶν ἀνθρώπων λαμβάνομεν, ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ θεοῦ μείζων ἐστίν, ὅτι αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ θεοῦ ὅτι μεμαρτύρηκεν περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: If the testimony of the human beings we receive, the testimony of the God greater is, because this is the testimony of the God, that he has testified about the Son of him.

en.L: If we receive the testimony of {{gender:human beings|men}}, the testimony of God is greater, because this is the testimony of God, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has testified about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son.
en.B: We accept the testimony of {{gender:people|men}}; the testimony of God is greater, for this is the testimony God has given: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has testified about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son.
en.R: We believe what {{gender:people|men}} tell us when they are witnesses. But what God tells us is far more important. And God has told us about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son.

es.L: Si recibimos el testimonio de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}, el testimonio de Dios es mayor, porque este es el testimonio de Dios: que ha dado testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo.
es.B: Aceptamos el testimonio de {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}; el testimonio de Dios es mayor, pues este es el testimonio que Dios ha dado: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha dado testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo.
es.R: Creemos lo que nos dicen {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} cuando son testigos. Pero lo que Dios nos dice es mucho más importante. Y Dios nos ha hablado acerca de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo.

fr.L: Si nous recevons le témoignage {{gender:des humains|des hommes}}, le témoignage de Dieu est plus grand, parce que ceci est le témoignage de Dieu : qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a rendu témoignage au sujet de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils.
fr.B: Nous acceptons le témoignage {{gender:des humains|des hommes}} ; le témoignage de Dieu est plus grand, car voici le témoignage que Dieu a rendu : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a rendu témoignage à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils.
fr.R: Nous croyons ce que {{gender:les gens|les hommes}} nous disent quand ils sont témoins. Mais ce que Dieu nous dit est bien plus important. Et Dieu nous a parlé de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils.

sw.L: Ikiwa tunaupokea ushuhuda wa wanadamu, ushuhuda wa Mungu ni mkuu zaidi, kwa sababu huu ndio ushuhuda wa Mungu, kwamba ameshuhudia kuhusu Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Tunaukubali ushuhuda wa wanadamu; ushuhuda wa Mungu ni mkuu kuliko huo, kwa maana ushuhuda ambao Mungu ametoa ni huu: ameshuhudia kuhusu Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Tunaamini yale ambayo watu wanatuambia wanapokuwa mashahidi. Lakini yale ambayo Mungu anatuambia ni muhimu zaidi sana. Naye Mungu ametuambia habari za Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

ko.L: 우리가 사람들의 증언을 받아들인다면, 하나님의 증언은 더 큽니다. 하나님의 증언은 이것이니, 곧 그분이 자기 아들에 대하여 증언하셨다는 것입니다.
ko.B: 우리는 사람들의 증언도 받아들입니다. 그러나 하나님의 증언은 더 큽니다. 하나님께서 주신 증언은 이것입니다. 그분이 자기 아들에 대해 증언하셨습니다.
ko.R: 우리는 사람들이 증인이 되어 하는 말을 믿습니다. 그러나 하나님께서 우리에게 하시는 말씀은 훨씬 더 중요합니다. 그리고 하나님께서는 그분의 아들에 대해 우리에게 말씀하셨습니다.

vi.L: Nếu chúng ta nhận lời chứng của loài người, thì lời chứng của Đức Chúa Trời còn lớn hơn, vì đây là lời chứng của Đức Chúa Trời: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm chứng về Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Chúng ta vẫn nhận lời chứng của loài người; lời chứng của Đức Chúa Trời còn lớn hơn, vì đây là lời chứng Đức Chúa Trời đã ban: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm chứng về Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Chúng ta tin điều người ta nói với mình khi họ làm chứng. Nhưng điều Đức Chúa Trời nói với chúng ta còn quan trọng hơn nhiều. Và Đức Chúa Trời đã làm chứng với chúng ta về Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: if, as we do: a condition assumed to be true
alternatives: if, as may or may not be the case
decisions.reason: The condition states a fact: people do accept human witnesses, as the law requires (Deuteronomy 19:15). The argument goes from the lesser to the greater.

decisions.choice: this is God's testimony: that he has testified about his Son
alternatives: because he has testified about his Son
decisions.reason: The first ὅτι gives the reason God's testimony applies here; the second (ὅτι) states what the testimony is. The perfect μεμαρτύρηκεν means his testimony was given and still stands. It is the witness of verses 6-8, and verses 10-11 say what it contains.

decisions.choice: human beings, men and women
decisions.reason: The plural is general, so the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: that he has testified (SBLGNT)
alternatives: which he has testified (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the Textus Receptus, read a relative pronoun ("which he has testified") in place of ὅτι. The sense is close, so no footnote. A reviewer should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: no "if": We accept ...
decisions.reason: English "if" suggests doubt; Balanced states the fact the condition assumes (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "if".

decisions.choice: what people tell us when they are witnesses ... far more important
decisions.reason: Readable explains "testimony" as what a witness tells and "greater" as more important and more trustworthy. It leaves out the explanatory "this is God's testimony" and says what it is.

decisions.choice: ha dado testimonio, no span
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun unsaid, so where the English has "he" for God there is often no Spanish word for the deity_pronoun setting to capitalise. A span goes only where a pronoun is written, as in Balanced "{{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha dado testimonio".

decisions.choice: wanadamu (L, B), watu (R), no gender span
decisions.reason: "Wanadamu" and "watu" already mean human beings, men and women (m3); "wanaume" means males and would change the meaning, so Swahili has no counterpart to the English gender span.

decisions.choice: "사람들" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, men and women (meaning decision); Korean "사람" has no generic masculine, so the setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: "loài người", "người ta", with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "loài người" and "người ta" are already inclusive, so the setting has no second wording to offer.

source.text: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ἔχει τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἐν αὑτῷ· ὁ μὴ πιστεύων τῷ θεῷ ψεύστην πεποίηκεν αὐτόν, ὅτι οὐ πεπίστευκεν εἰς τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἣν μεμαρτύρηκεν ὁ θεὸς περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] believing into the Son of the God has the testimony in himself; the [one] not believing the God a liar has made him, because not he has believed into the testimony which has testified the God about the Son of him.

en.L: The one who believes in the Son of God has the testimony in {{gender:themselves|himself}}; the one who does not believe God has made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a liar, because {{gender:they have|he has}} not believed in the testimony that God has testified about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son.
en.B: Whoever believes in the Son of God has this testimony within. Whoever does not believe God has made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a liar, by refusing to believe the testimony God has given about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son.
en.R: If you believe in the Son of God, you have God's testimony in your own heart. If you do not believe God, you are calling {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a liar. You have not believed what God has said about {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son.

es.L: Quien cree en el Hijo de Dios tiene dentro de sí el testimonio; quien no cree a Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha hecho mentiroso, porque no ha creído en el testimonio que ha dado Dios acerca de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo.
es.B: Quien cree en el Hijo de Dios lleva dentro este testimonio. Quien no cree a Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha hecho pasar por mentiroso, al negarse a creer el testimonio que Dios ha dado sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo.
es.R: Si crees en el Hijo de Dios, tienes en tu propio corazón el testimonio de Dios. Si no le crees a Dios, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} estás llamando mentiroso. No has creído lo que Dios ha dicho acerca de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo.

fr.L: Celui qui croit au Fils de Dieu a le témoignage en lui-même ; celui qui ne croit pas Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a fait menteur, parce qu’il n’a pas cru au témoignage que Dieu a rendu au sujet de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils.
fr.B: Quiconque croit au Fils de Dieu porte ce témoignage en lui. Quiconque ne croit pas Dieu a fait de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} un menteur, en refusant de croire au témoignage que Dieu a rendu à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils.
fr.R: Si vous croyez au Fils de Dieu, vous avez le témoignage de Dieu au fond de votre cœur. Si vous ne croyez pas Dieu, vous dites qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est un menteur. Vous n’avez pas cru ce que Dieu a dit de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils.

sw.L: Yule anayemwamini Mwana wa Mungu ana ushuhuda huo ndani ya nafsi yake; yule asiyemwamini Mungu amemfanya {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kuwa mwongo, kwa sababu hajauamini ushuhuda alioutoa Mungu kuhusu Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Anayemwamini Mwana wa Mungu ana ushuhuda huu moyoni. Asiyemwamini Mungu amemfanya kuwa mwongo, kwa kukataa kuamini ushuhuda ambao Mungu ametoa kuhusu Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Ukimwamini Mwana wa Mungu, ushuhuda wa Mungu uko ndani ya moyo wako. Usipomwamini Mungu, unamwita mwongo. Hujaamini yale ambayo Mungu amesema kuhusu Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

ko.L: 하나님의 아들을 믿는 사람은 그 증언을 자기 안에 가지고 있습니다. 하나님을 믿지 않는 사람은 그분을 거짓말쟁이로 만들었습니다. 하나님께서 자기 아들에 대하여 증언하신 그 증언을 믿지 않았기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 하나님의 아들을 믿는 사람은 이 증언을 마음속에 가지고 있습니다. 하나님을 믿지 않는 사람은 하나님을 거짓말쟁이로 만든 것입니다. 하나님께서 자기 아들에 대해 하신 증언을 믿지 않았기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 여러분이 하나님의 아들을 믿는다면, 여러분은 하나님의 증언을 여러분 마음속에 가지고 있는 것입니다. 여러분이 하나님을 믿지 않는다면, 하나님을 거짓말쟁이라고 하는 것입니다. 하나님께서 그분의 아들에 대해 하신 말씀을 믿지 않은 것입니다.

vi.L: Người tin vào Con Đức Chúa Trời thì có lời chứng ấy trong mình; người không tin Đức Chúa Trời thì đã làm cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thành kẻ nói dối, vì không tin vào lời chứng Đức Chúa Trời đã làm chứng về Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Ai tin vào Con Đức Chúa Trời thì có lời chứng ấy ở trong mình. Ai không tin Đức Chúa Trời thì đã cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là kẻ nói dối, vì không chịu tin lời chứng Đức Chúa Trời đã làm về Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Nếu các con tin vào Con Đức Chúa Trời, các con có lời chứng của Đức Chúa Trời trong lòng mình. Nếu ai không tin Đức Chúa Trời, người ấy đang cho rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là kẻ nói dối. Người ấy đã không tin điều Đức Chúa Trời nói về Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: in himself: the believer has God's testimony within
alternatives: in him, that is, in the Son
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads αὑτῷ with a rough breathing, the reflexive "himself": the one who believes has taken God's testimony inside, where it remains (compare 2:14, 24). Some manuscripts read "in him", which could refer to the Son. A reviewer should check the breathing and the variant against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: believe in the Son; believe God; believe in the testimony
decisions.reason: John uses "believe in" for trusting a person (the Son) and "believe" with a plain object for accepting what someone says (God). The last clause unusually says "believed in the testimony": not accepting what God says is refusing to trust him.

decisions.choice: to reject God's testimony is to call God a liar
decisions.reason: God has given his word about his Son; refusing it treats him as one who lies, as 1:10 says of those who deny they have sinned.

decisions.choice: does not believe God (SBLGNT)
alternatives: does not believe the Son (some manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "the Son" in place of "God", in line with the first half of the verse. A reviewer should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: whoever (B); if you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the general "whoever" and avoids a pronoun for the believer; Readable speaks to the reader directly, which keeps the general sense in plain words.

decisions.choice: in your own heart
decisions.reason: Readable says where the testimony is kept, using the ordinary image for the inner person.

decisions.choice: dentro de sí, no gender span
alternatives: en sí mismo o en sí misma
decisions.reason: "Dentro de sí" does not mark gender, so the English span for "themselves|himself" has no Spanish counterpart; "quien" already covers men and women.

decisions.choice: si crees ... tienes (tú), no plural_you
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to any one reader, as the English Readable's "if you" does. Spanish uses the general singular "tú" for this, which does not change between Latin America and Spain, so there is no plural_you span.

decisions.choice: "en lui-même", "il n’a pas cru" with no gender span (and the same for "il", "le" referring to the believer in 5:16 and 5:18)
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:themselves|himself}} and {{gender:they have|he has}} for the generic believer. In French these pronouns refer back to "celui qui", which already means anyone, so as the style guide says they are ordinary generic French and take no setting.

decisions.choice: "Si vous croyez" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the reader directly, as the English does. John writes to the readers as a group ("vous" throughout the letter), so French uses "vous" rather than a generic "tu".

decisions.choice: amemfanya yeye kuwa mwongo
decisions.reason: Literal writes the free pronoun "yeye" for the Greek pronoun, which makes plain that it is God who is made a liar (m3) and carries the deity_pronoun span. Balanced leaves the pronoun in the verb, as ordinary Swahili does.

decisions.choice: "tin vào" for believe in (eis), "tin" for believe God
decisions.reason: The verse uses three constructions (m2). The style guide sets "tin vào" for the construction with eis and plain "tin" otherwise, so the difference stays visible.

source.text: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία, ὅτι ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἔδωκεν ὁ θεὸς ἡμῖν, καὶ αὕτη ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: And this is the testimony, that life eternal gave the God to us, and this the life in the Son of him is.

en.L: And this is the testimony: that eternal life God gave to us, and this life is in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son.
en.B: And here is what the testimony says: God gave us eternal life, and that life is found in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son.
en.R: This is what God's testimony says: God has given us eternal life, and this life is found in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son.

es.L: Y este es el testimonio: que vida eterna nos dio Dios, y esta vida está en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo.
es.B: Y esto es lo que dice el testimonio: Dios nos dio vida eterna, y esa vida se encuentra en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice el testimonio de Dios: Dios nos ha dado vida eterna, y esta vida se encuentra en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo.

fr.L: Et ceci est le témoignage : que Dieu nous a donné la vie éternelle, et cette vie est dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils.
fr.B: Et voici ce que dit ce témoignage : Dieu nous a donné la vie éternelle, et cette vie se trouve dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit le témoignage de Dieu : Dieu nous a donné la vie éternelle, et cette vie, on la trouve dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils.

sw.L: Na huu ndio ushuhuda, kwamba uzima wa milele Mungu alitupa, na uzima huu uko ndani ya Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Na hiki ndicho ushuhuda unachosema: Mungu alitupa uzima wa milele, na uzima huo unapatikana ndani ya Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Hiki ndicho ushuhuda wa Mungu unachosema: Mungu ametupa uzima wa milele, na uzima huu unapatikana ndani ya Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그 증언은 이것이니, 곧 하나님께서 우리에게 영원한 생명을 주셨고, 이 생명이 그분의 아들 안에 있다는 것입니다.
ko.B: 그 증언은 이것입니다. 하나님께서 우리에게 영원한 생명을 주셨고, 그 생명은 그분의 아들 안에 있습니다.
ko.R: 하나님의 증언은 이것입니다. 하나님께서 우리에게 영원한 생명을 주셨고, 이 생명은 그분의 아들 안에 있습니다.

vi.L: Và đây là lời chứng: Đức Chúa Trời đã ban cho chúng ta sự sống đời đời, và sự sống ấy ở trong Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Và đây là điều lời chứng ấy nói: Đức Chúa Trời đã ban cho chúng ta sự sống đời đời, và sự sống ấy ở trong Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đây là điều lời chứng của Đức Chúa Trời nói: Đức Chúa Trời đã ban cho chúng ta sự sống đời đời, và sự sống này ở trong Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

decisions.choice: eternal life: the life of God himself, given now and lasting forever
alternatives: life that only begins after death
decisions.reason: Key term. In John's writings eternal life is the life that was with the Father and appeared in Jesus (1:2), given to believers now (5:12-13; John 5:24) and never ending.

decisions.choice: God gave: a gift given once, which believers now have
decisions.reason: The aorist ἔδωκεν looks at the giving as a completed act; verse 12 says the believer now has the life.

decisions.choice: the life is in the Son: it is had only by having him
decisions.reason: The life is not a thing God hands over apart from the Son; it is in him, so to have the Son is to have the life (verse 12; John 1:4; 14:6).

decisions.choice: is found in
decisions.reason: "Found" makes clear that the Son is where the life is (meaning decision m3); Literal keeps "is in".

decisions.choice: uzima wa milele
decisions.reason: As in John's Gospel: "maisha" is a lifetime or daily living, while "uzima" is life itself, the life of God given now (m1).

source.text: ὁ ἔχων τὸν υἱὸν ἔχει τὴν ζωήν· ὁ μὴ ἔχων τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν ζωὴν οὐκ ἔχει.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] having the Son has the life; the [one] not having the Son of the God the life not has.

en.L: The one who has the Son has the life; the one who does not have the Son of God does not have the life.
en.B: Anyone who has the Son has the life; anyone without the Son of God does not have the life.
en.R: People who have the Son have this life. People who do not have the Son of God do not have this life.

es.L: El que tiene al Hijo tiene la vida; el que no tiene al Hijo de Dios, la vida no [la] tiene.
es.B: Todo el que tiene al Hijo tiene la vida; el que está sin el Hijo de Dios no tiene la vida.
es.R: Las personas que tienen al Hijo tienen esta vida. Las que no tienen al Hijo de Dios no tienen esta vida.

fr.L: Celui qui a le Fils a la vie ; celui qui n’a pas le Fils de Dieu n’a pas la vie.
fr.B: Quiconque a le Fils a la vie ; quiconque est sans le Fils de Dieu n’a pas la vie.
fr.R: Ceux qui ont le Fils ont cette vie. Ceux qui n’ont pas le Fils de Dieu n’ont pas cette vie.

sw.L: Mwenye Mwana anao uzima; asiye na Mwana wa Mungu, uzima hanao.
sw.B: Kila aliye na Mwana anao uzima huo; asiye na Mwana wa Mungu hana uzima huo.
sw.R: Watu walio na Mwana wana uzima huu. Watu wasio na Mwana wa Mungu hawana uzima huu.

ko.L: 아들을 모신 사람은 생명을 가지고 있고, 하나님의 아들을 모시지 않은 사람은 생명을 가지고 있지 않습니다.
ko.B: 아들을 모신 사람에게는 생명이 있고, 하나님의 아들을 모시지 않은 사람에게는 생명이 없습니다.
ko.R: 아들을 모신 사람은 이 생명을 가지고 있습니다. 하나님의 아들을 모시지 않은 사람은 이 생명을 가지고 있지 않습니다.

vi.L: Ai có Con thì có sự sống; ai không có Con Đức Chúa Trời thì không có sự sống.
vi.B: Ai có Con thì có sự sống; ai không có Con Đức Chúa Trời thì không có sự sống.
vi.R: Những ai có Con thì có sự sống này. Những ai không có Con Đức Chúa Trời thì không có sự sống này.

decisions.choice: the life: the eternal life just named in verse 11
decisions.reason: Both times the noun has the article, which points back to "this life" in verse 11.

decisions.choice: to have the Son: to belong to him by believing in him
alternatives: to know facts about the Son
decisions.reason: "Having" the Son, as in 2:23 ("having the Father") and 2 John 9, means being joined to him in a living relationship, which comes by believing (verses 10 and 13).

decisions.choice: the life (L, B); this life (R)
decisions.reason: The article is kept so that the reader hears that the life meant is the eternal life of verse 11 (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: uzima huo
decisions.reason: Swahili has no article, and the Greek article points back to the eternal life of verse 11 (m1). Balanced says "uzima huo" (that life) to keep the link; Readable says "uzima huu", as the English Readable says "this life".

decisions.choice: "모시다" for having the Son, as in 2:23; "가지다" for having life
decisions.reason: To have the Son is to belong to him by believing in him (meaning decision). Korean cannot say "가지다" respectfully of a person, so the Son is "모시다", as the Father in 2:23, while life, which is not a person, is "가지다".

source.text: Ταῦτα ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ἵνα εἰδῆτε ὅτι ζωὴν ἔχετε αἰώνιον, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: These things I wrote to you so that you may know that life you have eternal, to the [ones] believing into the name of the Son of the God.

en.L: These things I wrote to you so that you may know that you have life eternal, to you who believe in the name of the Son of God.
en.B: I have written these things to you so that you may know that you have eternal life—you who believe in the name of the Son of God.
en.R: You believe in the Son of God. I have written this letter to you so that you can know for sure that you have eternal life.

es.L: Estas cosas {{plural_you:les|os}} escribí para que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} vida eterna, a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los que {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} en el nombre del Hijo de Dios.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he escrito estas cosas para que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} vida eterna, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} en el nombre del Hijo de Dios.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} en el Hijo de Dios. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he escrito esta carta para que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} con seguridad que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} vida eterna.

fr.L: Je vous ai écrit ces choses afin que vous sachiez que vous avez la vie éternelle, à vous qui croyez au nom du Fils de Dieu.
fr.B: Je vous ai écrit cela pour que vous sachiez que vous avez la vie éternelle, vous qui croyez au nom du Fils de Dieu.
fr.R: Vous croyez au Fils de Dieu. Je vous ai écrit cette lettre pour que vous sachiez avec certitude que vous avez la vie éternelle.

sw.L: Mambo haya niliwaandikia ili mjue kwamba mnao uzima wa milele, ninyi mnaoamini katika jina la Mwana wa Mungu.
sw.B: Nimewaandikia mambo haya ili mjue kwamba mna uzima wa milele, ninyi mnaoamini katika jina la Mwana wa Mungu.
sw.R: Ninyi mnamwamini Mwana wa Mungu. Nimewaandikia barua hii ili mjue kwa hakika kwamba mna uzima wa milele.

ko.L: 내가 하나님의 아들의 이름을 믿는 여러분에게 이것들을 쓴 것은, 여러분이 영원한 생명을 가지고 있다는 것을 알게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 하나님의 아들의 이름을 믿는 여러분에게 내가 이것을 쓴 것은, 여러분에게 영원한 생명이 있다는 것을 여러분이 알게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.R: 여러분은 하나님의 아들을 믿습니다. 내가 여러분에게 이 편지를 쓴 것은, 여러분에게 영원한 생명이 있다는 것을 여러분이 확실히 알게 하려는 것입니다.

vi.L: Tôi đã viết những điều này cho các con, để các con biết rằng mình có sự sống đời đời, cho các con là những người tin vào danh Con Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Tôi đã viết những điều này cho các con để các con biết rằng mình có sự sống đời đời, là các con, những người tin vào danh Con Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Các con tin vào Con Đức Chúa Trời. Tôi đã viết thư này cho các con để các con biết chắc rằng mình có sự sống đời đời.

decisions.choice: these things I have written: the letter as a whole, and especially 5:1-12
decisions.reason: ἔγραψα is an aorist written from the reader's point of view: by the time they read it, the writing is done. "These things" naturally takes in the letter and sums up its purpose, though it follows closely on 5:1-12.

decisions.choice: an echo of John 20:31
decisions.reason: John's Gospel states its purpose in similar words: written so that you may believe and have life in his name. The letter is written to those who already believe, so that they may know they have that life.

decisions.choice: believe in the name: believe in the person
decisions.reason: In Hebrew thought a name stands for the person (as in John 1:12).

decisions.choice: the short text (SBLGNT)
alternatives: a longer text in many later manuscripts and the Textus Receptus, which places "to you who believe in the name of the Son of God" earlier and adds at the end "and so that you may believe in the name of the Son of God"
decisions.reason: The longer wording, found in the King James Version, repeats the phrase about believing in the name and appears to expand the sentence. The SBLGNT follows earlier manuscripts with the shorter text. A reviewer should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the phrase about believers placed last, after a dash
alternatives: to you who believe ... placed first
decisions.reason: The Greek adds "to the ones who believe" at the end; Balanced keeps it there.

decisions.choice: this letter; know for sure
decisions.reason: Readable says what "these things" are (meaning decision m1) and uses "know for sure" for a verb that means knowing with certainty, which is the point of the sentence. It puts the description of the readers first, as its own sentence.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: John writes to his readers in the plural. Each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), as in John's Gospel and the other letters.

source.text: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ παρρησία ἣν ἔχομεν πρὸς αὐτόν, ὅτι ἐάν τι αἰτώμεθα κατὰ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ἀκούει ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And this is the boldness which we have toward him, that if anything we ask according to the will of him he hears us.

en.L: And this is the boldness that we have toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: that if we ask something according to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hears us.
en.B: And here is the boldness we have in coming to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: whenever we ask for something in line with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} listens to us.
en.R: We can come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} without fear. If we ask for anything that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} listens to us.

es.L: Y esta es la libertad que tenemos ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: que si pedimos algo según {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voluntad, nos oye.
es.B: Y esta es la confianza con que nos acercamos a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: siempre que pedimos algo de acuerdo con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voluntad, nos escucha.
es.R: Podemos acercarnos a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sin miedo. Si pedimos algo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quiere, nos escucha.

fr.L: Et ceci est la hardiesse que nous avons envers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : que si nous demandons quelque chose selon {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} volonté, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous entend.
fr.B: Et voici la confiance avec laquelle nous nous approchons de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : chaque fois que nous demandons quelque chose qui est conforme à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} volonté, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous écoute.
fr.R: Nous pouvons venir vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} sans avoir peur. Si nous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demandons quelque chose qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} veut, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous écoute.

sw.L: Na huu ndio uhuru tulio nao mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kwamba tukiomba kitu chochote kufuatana na mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, anatusikia.
sw.B: Tunapomkaribia tunakuwa na ujasiri huu: kila tunapoomba jambo linalopatana na mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hutusikiliza.
sw.R: Tunaweza kumkaribia bila hofu. Tukiomba chochote anachotaka {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, anatusikiliza.

ko.L: 그리고 우리가 그분을 향하여 가진 담대함은 이것이니, 곧 우리가 그분의 뜻을 따라 무엇을 구하면 그분이 우리의 말을 들으신다는 것입니다.
ko.B: 우리가 그분께 나아갈 때 가지는 담대함은 이것입니다. 우리가 그분의 뜻에 맞게 무엇을 구하면, 그분은 우리의 말을 들어 주십니다.
ko.R: 우리는 두려움 없이 그분께 나아갈 수 있습니다. 우리가 그분이 원하시는 것을 구하면, 그분은 우리의 말을 들어 주십니다.

vi.L: Và đây là sự dạn dĩ chúng ta có đối với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: nếu chúng ta cầu xin điều gì theo ý muốn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghe chúng ta.
vi.B: Và đây là sự dạn dĩ chúng ta có khi đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: mỗi khi chúng ta cầu xin điều gì theo ý muốn của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lắng nghe chúng ta.
vi.R: Chúng ta có thể đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà không sợ hãi. Nếu chúng ta cầu xin bất cứ điều gì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lắng nghe chúng ta.

decisions.choice: boldness, freedom to speak openly
decisions.reason: παρρησία is the freedom to speak plainly and without fear, here before God. In 2:28 and 4:17 it is the boldness of believers on the day of judgment; in 3:21-22 and here it is boldness in prayer.

decisions.choice: him: God, to whom prayer is made
alternatives: the Son of God, named in verse 13
decisions.reason: In 3:21-22 the same boldness in asking is "before God", and asking according to "his will" fits God the Father. The pronoun could also refer to the Son, the last person named, and in John 14:14 Jesus speaks of being asked in his name. The levels keep the pronoun.

decisions.choice: asking in line with God's will is the condition, not a limit on God's hearing
decisions.reason: The sentence does not promise that any request will be granted, but that God hears every request made in keeping with his will. 3:22 adds keeping his commandments and doing what pleases him.

decisions.choice: hears us: listens with favor
decisions.reason: As in John 9:31 and 11:41-42, God's hearing means he attends to the request and grants it; verse 15 says so.

decisions.choice: listens to us
decisions.reason: "Listens" carries the sense of meaning decision m4 better than "hears", which can mean only that sound reaches the ear. Literal keeps "hears".

decisions.choice: We can come to him without fear
alternatives: this is the boldness we have toward him
decisions.reason: Readable explains "boldness" (meaning decision m1) as approaching God without fear.

decisions.choice: libertad (L); confianza (B); sin miedo (R)
decisions.reason: The word is freedom to speak openly (m1). Literal says "libertad" to keep that; Balanced says "confianza", the trust with which one comes before God; Readable says what it means in practice, as the English Readable does. "Osadía" would sound like rashness.

decisions.choice: la hardiesse (L); la confiance avec laquelle nous nous approchons (B)
decisions.reason: The word means boldness, freedom to speak openly (meaning decision m1). "Hardiesse" says that at Literal; Balanced says what the boldness is for, coming to God with confidence, as the English "in coming to him" does. "Assurance" in modern French more often means certainty, or insurance.

decisions.choice: uhuru (L); ujasiri (B); bila hofu (R)
decisions.reason: The word is freedom to speak openly (m1). Literal says "uhuru" (freedom) to keep that; Balanced says "ujasiri" (boldness) in coming to God; Readable says what it means in practice, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀκούει ἡμῶν ὃ ἐὰν αἰτώμεθα, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἔχομεν τὰ αἰτήματα ἃ ᾐτήκαμεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And if we know that he hears us whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests which we have asked from him.

en.L: And if we know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hears us, whatever we ask, we know that we have the requests that we have asked from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: And if we know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hears us in whatever we ask, we know that the requests we have made of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} are ours.
en.R: Since we know {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} listens to us whenever we ask, we also know that what we asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for is ours.

es.L: Y si sabemos que nos oye, pidamos lo que pidamos, sabemos que tenemos las peticiones que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hemos presentado.
es.B: Y si sabemos que nos escucha en todo lo que pedimos, sabemos que ya son nuestras las peticiones que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hemos hecho.
es.R: Como sabemos que nos escucha siempre que pedimos, también sabemos que lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hemos pedido ya es nuestro.

fr.L: Et si nous savons qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous entend, quoi que nous demandions, nous savons que nous avons les demandes que nous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} avons faites.
fr.B: Et si nous savons qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous entend dans tout ce que nous demandons, nous savons que les demandes que nous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} avons présentées sont déjà à nous.
fr.R: Puisque nous savons qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous écoute chaque fois que nous demandons, nous savons aussi que ce que nous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} avons demandé est à nous.

sw.L: Na ikiwa tunajua kwamba anatusikia, chochote tunachoomba, tunajua kwamba tunayo maombi tuliyoyaomba kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: Na ikiwa tunajua kwamba anatusikia katika chochote tunachoomba, tunajua kwamba maombi tuliyomwomba ni yetu.
sw.R: Kwa kuwa tunajua kwamba anatusikiliza kila tunapoomba, tunajua pia kwamba kile tulichomwomba ni chetu.

ko.L: 그리고 우리가 무엇을 구하든지 그분이 우리의 말을 들으신다는 것을 알면, 우리는 우리가 그분께 구한 것들을 가지고 있다는 것을 압니다.
ko.B: 그리고 우리가 무엇을 구하든지 그분이 우리의 말을 들으신다는 것을 알면, 우리가 그분께 구한 것들이 이미 우리의 것이라는 것도 압니다.
ko.R: 우리가 구할 때마다 그분이 들어 주신다는 것을 알기 때문에, 우리가 그분께 구한 것이 이미 우리의 것이라는 것도 압니다.

vi.L: Và nếu chúng ta biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghe chúng ta, bất cứ điều gì chúng ta cầu xin, thì chúng ta biết rằng chúng ta đã có những điều mình đã cầu xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Và nếu chúng ta biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghe chúng ta trong bất cứ điều gì chúng ta cầu xin, thì chúng ta biết rằng những điều mình đã cầu xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là của chúng ta.
vi.R: Vì chúng ta biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lắng nghe mỗi khi chúng ta cầu xin, chúng ta cũng biết rằng những gì mình đã xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là của mình rồi.

decisions.choice: if, as is the case: since we know
decisions.reason: ἐὰν usually takes a subjunctive; here it takes the indicative οἴδαμεν, so it works like "if" stating a fact: since we know.

decisions.choice: we have the requests: they are already ours, though not yet seen
alternatives: we will receive the requests later
decisions.reason: The present ἔχομεν says that what was asked is already possessed; the answer is certain, even if it comes later.

decisions.choice: Since
decisions.reason: Readable states the fact the condition assumes (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἐάν τις ἴδῃ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτάνοντα ἁμαρτίαν μὴ πρὸς θάνατον, αἰτήσει, καὶ δώσει αὐτῷ ζωήν, τοῖς ἁμαρτάνουσιν μὴ πρὸς θάνατον.

records.literal_gloss: If anyone sees the brother of him sinning a sin not toward death, he will ask, and he will give to him life, to the [ones] sinning not toward death.

en.L: If anyone sees {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} sinning a sin not to death, {{gender:they|he}} will ask, and [God] will give {{gender:them|him}} life, to those who sin not to death.
en.B: If anyone sees {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} committing a sin that does not lead to death, {{gender:they|he}} should ask, and God will give that person life. This is for those whose sin does not lead to death.
en.R: If anyone sees a fellow believer doing something sinful that does not lead to death, {{gender:they|he}} should pray for that believer, and God will give that person life. This is for people whose sin does not lead to death.

es.L: Si alguien ve a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}} pecando con un pecado no para muerte, pedirá, y [Dios] le dará vida, a los que pecan no para muerte.
es.B: Si alguien ve a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}} cometer un pecado que no lleva a la muerte, debe pedir, y Dios le dará vida a esa persona. Esto vale para aquellos cuyo pecado no lleva a la muerte.
es.R: Si alguien ve que {{gender:un hermano o una hermana en la fe|un hermano en la fe}} hace algo malo que no lleva a la muerte, debe orar por esa persona, y Dios le dará vida. Esto es para las personas cuyo pecado no lleva a la muerte.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un voit {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} pécher d’un péché [qui ne conduit] pas à la mort, il demandera, et [Dieu] lui donnera la vie, à ceux qui pèchent [d’un péché qui ne conduit] pas à la mort.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un voit {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}} commettre un péché qui ne conduit pas à la mort, qu’il demande, et Dieu donnera la vie à cette personne. Cela vaut pour ceux dont le péché ne conduit pas à la mort.
fr.R: Si quelqu’un voit {{gender:un frère ou une sœur|un frère}} dans la foi commettre un péché qui ne conduit pas à la mort, il doit prier pour cette personne, et Dieu lui donnera la vie. C’est pour ceux dont le péché ne conduit pas à la mort.

sw.L: Mtu yeyote akimwona ndugu yake akitenda dhambi isiyoelekea kifo, ataomba, na [Mungu] atampa uzima, kwa wale wanaotenda dhambi isiyoelekea kifo.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote akimwona ndugu yake akitenda dhambi isiyoleta kifo, na aombe, naye Mungu atampa mtu huyo uzima. Hili ni kwa ajili ya wale ambao dhambi yao haileti kifo.
sw.R: Mtu yeyote akimwona mwamini mwenzake akifanya dhambi isiyoleta kifo, na amwombee mwamini huyo, naye Mungu atampa mtu huyo uzima. Hili ni kwa ajili ya watu ambao dhambi yao haileti kifo.

ko.L: 누구든지 자기 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}가 죽음에 이르지 않는 죄를 짓는 것을 보면, 그는 구할 것이고, [하나님께서] 그에게 생명을 주실 것입니다. 죽음에 이르지 않는 죄를 짓는 사람들에게 [그렇게 하실 것입니다].
ko.B: 누구든지 자기 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}가 죽음에 이르지 않는 죄를 짓는 것을 보면, 그를 위해 구해야 합니다. 그러면 하나님께서 그 사람에게 생명을 주실 것입니다. 이것은 죽음에 이르지 않는 죄를 짓는 사람들을 두고 하는 말입니다.
ko.R: 누구든지 믿음의 식구가 죽음에 이르지 않는 죄를 짓는 것을 보면, 그 사람을 위해 기도해야 합니다. 그러면 하나님께서 그 사람에게 생명을 주실 것입니다. 이것은 죽음에 이르지 않는 죄를 짓는 사람들을 두고 하는 말입니다.

vi.L: Nếu ai thấy {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} mình phạm tội không đến nỗi chết, thì người ấy sẽ cầu xin, và [Đức Chúa Trời] sẽ ban sự sống cho người kia, tức là cho những người phạm tội không đến nỗi chết.
vi.B: Nếu ai thấy {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} mình phạm một tội không dẫn đến sự chết, người ấy nên cầu xin, và Đức Chúa Trời sẽ ban sự sống cho người phạm tội ấy. Điều này dành cho những người phạm tội không dẫn đến sự chết.
vi.R: Nếu ai thấy một anh chị em cùng đức tin làm điều tội lỗi không dẫn đến sự chết, người ấy nên cầu nguyện cho anh chị em đó, và Đức Chúa Trời sẽ ban sự sống cho người ấy. Điều này dành cho những người phạm tội không dẫn đến sự chết.

decisions.choice: sin not leading to death: sin that does not cut a person off from life
alternatives: sin that does not cause bodily death
decisions.reason: The phrase means, word for word, sin "toward death": sin that leads to death. The letter does not say what that sin is, whether the death is the loss of eternal life or bodily death, or how another believer would recognize it. In the letter, "life" is eternal life (5:11-13) and its opposite is remaining in death (3:14), so many take the sin leading to death as the refusal of Jesus that marks those who left the community (2:19, 22-23; 4:1-3; 5:10-12): rejecting the Son is rejecting the life that is in him. Others think of deliberate, persistent sin, as in the Old Testament contrast between unintentional sins and sins "with a high hand" (Numbers 15:27-31), or of sins that God punished with death (Acts 5:1-11; 1 Corinthians 11:30). The text does not settle the question, so a footnote names the readings.

decisions.choice: he will ask: a future that works as an instruction (he should ask)
decisions.reason: The future αἰτήσει, in the main clause after "if", here states what should happen, as futures often do in commands. The asking is the prayer of verses 14-15.

decisions.choice: God will give life to the one who sinned
alternatives: the one who prays will give him life (through the prayer)
decisions.reason: Grammatically the subject of δώσει is most naturally the same as that of "will ask": the one who prays. But life is God's gift (5:11), so the one who prays gives it only as the means through which God gives it. Either way, God is the source of the life and the sinner receives it; the levels name God as the giver.

decisions.choice: brother or sister: a fellow believer
decisions.reason: In 1 John ἀδελφός means a fellow member of the believing community, man or woman, so the gender setting applies (as in 2:9-11; 3:14-17; 4:20-21).

decisions.choice: {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} ... {{gender:they|he}} ... {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: Inclusive default, traditional one tap away. Readable says "a fellow believer" and "that believer", which need no setting; only its pronoun for "anyone" takes one.

decisions.choice: [God] (L); God (B, R)
decisions.reason: The levels name the giver (meaning decision m3); Literal marks the word as supplied.

decisions.choice: pray for that believer
decisions.reason: "Ask" is the word for prayer in verses 14-15; Readable says "pray" so the young reader knows who is asked and for whom.

decisions.choice: {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}}; no span for "they|he"
decisions.reason: The plural "hermanos" covers men and women, but the singular "su hermano" names a man, and John means any fellow believer (m4), so the singular takes the gender setting, as in James 1:9. Spanish leaves the subject of "pedirá" unsaid and "le" does not change, so the English spans for "they|he" and "them|him" need no Spanish counterpart.

decisions.choice: no para muerte (L); que no lleva a la muerte (B, R)
decisions.reason: The preposition points toward death, sin that ends in death (m1). Literal keeps the bare phrase; Balanced and Readable say "que no lleva a la muerte", which keeps the direction and does not define the sin further than John does.

decisions.choice: "[qui ne conduit] pas à la mort" (L); "qui ne conduit pas à la mort" (B, R); the same in 5:16b and 5:17
alternatives: "qui ne mène pas à la mort"
decisions.reason: French cannot attach the bare phrase "not to death" to a noun as the Greek and the English Literal do; "pour la mort" would suggest a purpose. Literal supplies the verb in brackets; Balanced and Readable say "conduire à la mort", the English "lead to death".

decisions.choice: {{gender:un frère ou une sœur|un frère}} dans la foi (R)
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "a fellow believer", which is inclusive and needs no setting. French "un croyant" is masculine, so Readable keeps the family word with the gender setting, as the other levels do, and adds "dans la foi" to say who is meant (meaning decision m4). The pronoun "il" for "quelqu’un" takes no span.

decisions.choice: ndugu yake, no gender span
alternatives: ndugu yake wa kiume au wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brother or sister (m4), and Swahili verbs do not mark gender, so the English spans for "their brother or sister", "they" and "them" have no Swahili counterpart.

decisions.choice: isiyoelekea kifo (L); isiyoleta kifo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The preposition points toward death, sin that ends in death (m1). Literal keeps the direction with "kuelekea" (go toward); Balanced and Readable say "isiyoleta kifo" (that does not bring death). "Kifo" is the everyday word, and neither defines the sin further than John does.

decisions.choice: "죽음에 이르지 않는 죄" at every level; "[하나님께서] ... 주실 것입니다"
decisions.reason: The meaning decisions leave open what the two kinds of sin are and read God as the one who gives life, both footnoted. Korean "죽음에 이르다" is the plain phrase, kept the same in 5:16-17 so the contrast is visible; the honorific "주실" follows the meaning decision that God is the giver.

decisions.choice: "cầu xin" (L, B); "cầu nguyện cho" (R) for ask (also 5:16b)
decisions.reason: To ask here is to pray for the other person (m2), so Vietnamese uses "cầu xin", asking of God, as in 5:14-15; Readable says "pray", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "[Đức Chúa Trời]" and "người kia" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves both the giver and the receiver unnamed (m3); Literal names God in brackets, as the English does, and says "người kia", the other person, so the one who prays and the one who sinned are kept apart.

source.text: ἔστιν ἁμαρτία πρὸς θάνατον· οὐ περὶ ἐκείνης λέγω ἵνα ἐρωτήσῃ.

records.literal_gloss: There is sin toward death; not about that [one] do I say that he should ask.

en.L: There is sin to death; I do not say that one should make request about that.
en.B: There is sin that leads to death. I am not saying that anyone should make request about that.
en.R: There is sin that leads to death. I am not telling you to pray about that kind of sin.

es.L: Hay pecado para muerte; no digo que se haga petición acerca de ese.
es.B: Hay pecado que lleva a la muerte. No estoy diciendo que se haga petición por ese pecado.
es.R: Hay pecado que lleva a la muerte. No {{plural_you:les|os}} estoy diciendo que {{plural_you:oren|oréis}} por esa clase de pecado.

fr.L: Il y a un péché [qui conduit] à la mort ; ce n’est pas au sujet de celui-là que je dis de faire une requête.
fr.B: Il y a un péché qui conduit à la mort. Je ne dis pas qu’il faille adresser une requête à son sujet.
fr.R: Il y a un péché qui conduit à la mort. Je ne vous dis pas de prier pour ce genre de péché.

sw.L: Kuna dhambi inayoelekea kifo; si kuhusu hiyo ninasema kwamba aombe.
sw.B: Kuna dhambi inayoleta kifo. Sisemi kwamba mtu aombe kuhusu hiyo.
sw.R: Kuna dhambi inayoleta kifo. Siwaambii mwombe kuhusu dhambi ya aina hiyo.

ko.L: 죽음에 이르는 죄가 있습니다. 나는 그것에 대하여 구하라고 말하지 않습니다.
ko.B: 죽음에 이르는 죄가 있습니다. 나는 그런 죄에 대해 구하라고 말하는 것이 아닙니다.
ko.R: 죽음에 이르는 죄가 있습니다. 나는 그런 죄에 대해 기도하라고 말하는 것이 아닙니다.

vi.L: Có tội đến nỗi chết; tôi không nói về tội ấy mà bảo người ta nài xin.
vi.B: Có tội dẫn đến sự chết. Tôi không nói rằng phải cầu xin về tội ấy.
vi.R: Có tội dẫn đến sự chết. Tôi không bảo các con cầu nguyện về loại tội ấy.

decisions.choice: sin leading to death: not defined in the text
alternatives: apostasy, refusing Jesus as the Christ
a sin punished by bodily death
decisions.reason: The phrase means, word for word, sin "toward death": sin that leads to death. The letter does not say what that sin is, whether the death is the loss of eternal life or bodily death, or how another believer would recognize it. In the letter, "life" is eternal life (5:11-13) and its opposite is remaining in death (3:14), so many take the sin leading to death as the refusal of Jesus that marks those who left the community (2:19, 22-23; 4:1-3; 5:10-12): rejecting the Son is rejecting the life that is in him. Others think of deliberate, persistent sin, as in the Old Testament contrast between unintentional sins and sins "with a high hand" (Numbers 15:27-31), or of sins that God punished with death (Acts 5:1-11; 1 Corinthians 11:30). The text does not settle the question, so a footnote names the readings.

decisions.choice: John does not command prayer for it; he does not forbid it
alternatives: prayer for such a person is forbidden
decisions.reason: The words are "I do not say that he should ask". The writer gives no instruction for this case; he does not say that such prayer is wrong. He also changes the verb, from αἰτήσει in the previous sentence to ἐρωτήσῃ, which may mean making a request on someone's behalf; the difference is not clear.

decisions.choice: sin, without the article: sin of a kind
decisions.reason: ἁμαρτία has no article: the sentence speaks of a kind of sinning, not of one named act.

decisions.choice: make request (L, B); pray (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use a different word from "ask" in the previous sentence because the Greek changes the verb (meaning decision m2). Readable keeps "pray" as in the previous sentence.

decisions.choice: about that kind of sin
decisions.reason: Readable says what "that" refers to and keeps the sense that the text names a kind of sin (meaning decision m3).

source.text: πᾶσα ἀδικία ἁμαρτία ἐστίν, καὶ ἔστιν ἁμαρτία οὐ πρὸς θάνατον.

records.literal_gloss: All wrongdoing sin is, and there is sin not toward death.

en.L: All wrongdoing is sin, and there is sin not to death.
en.B: All wrongdoing is sin, and yet there is sin that does not lead to death.
en.R: Every wrong thing we do is sin. But not all sin leads to death.

es.L: Toda injusticia es pecado, y hay pecado no para muerte.
es.B: Todo lo que está mal hecho es pecado, y aun así hay pecado que no lleva a la muerte.
es.R: Todo lo malo que hacemos es pecado. Pero no todo pecado lleva a la muerte.

fr.L: Toute injustice est péché, et il y a un péché [qui ne conduit] pas à la mort.
fr.B: Toute forme de mal est péché, et pourtant il y a un péché qui ne conduit pas à la mort.
fr.R: Tout le mal que nous faisons est péché. Mais tout péché ne conduit pas à la mort.

sw.L: Kila udhalimu ni dhambi, na kuna dhambi isiyoelekea kifo.
sw.B: Kila kosa ni dhambi, na bado kuna dhambi isiyoleta kifo.
sw.R: Kila jambo baya tunalofanya ni dhambi. Lakini si kila dhambi inaleta kifo.

ko.L: 모든 불의는 죄입니다. 그러나 죽음에 이르지 않는 죄도 있습니다.
ko.B: 모든 불의는 죄입니다. 그러나 죽음에 이르지 않는 죄도 있습니다.
ko.R: 우리가 하는 모든 옳지 않은 일은 죄입니다. 그러나 모든 죄가 죽음에 이르는 것은 아닙니다.

vi.L: Mọi điều bất chính đều là tội, và có tội không đến nỗi chết.
vi.B: Mọi điều sai trái đều là tội, nhưng có tội không dẫn đến sự chết.
vi.R: Mọi điều sai trái chúng ta làm đều là tội. Nhưng không phải tội nào cũng dẫn đến sự chết.

decisions.choice: wrongdoing: any act that is not right
decisions.reason: ἀδικία is the opposite of doing what is right (1:9); the sentence warns that no wrong is harmless, even though not every sin leads to death.

decisions.choice: and yet: the second clause balances the first
decisions.reason: The verse holds two things together: all wrongdoing is sin and must be taken seriously, and yet sin not leading to death can be prayed for and forgiven (verse 16).

decisions.choice: not all sin leads to death
alternatives: there is sin that does not lead to death
decisions.reason: Readable restates the second clause in a simpler form that says the same thing.

decisions.choice: udhalimu (L); kosa (B)
decisions.reason: "Udhalimu" is the negative of right dealing and keeps the form of the Greek word at Literal. In everyday Swahili it often means oppression, which would narrow the sense (m1), so Balanced says "kosa", any wrong act.

source.text: Οἴδαμεν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ γεγεννημένος ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει, ἀλλ’ ὁ γεννηθεὶς ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ τηρεῖ αὐτόν, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς οὐχ ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: We know that everyone the having been born from the God not sins, but the [one] having been born from the God keeps him, and the evil [one] not touches him.

en.L: We know that everyone who has been born of God does not sin, but the one who was born of God keeps {{gender:them|him}}, and the evil one does not touch {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: We know that anyone born of God does not go on sinning; rather, the Son, who was born of God, keeps {{gender:them|him}} safe, and the evil one does not lay hold of {{gender:them|him}}.
en.R: We know that God's children do not keep on sinning. The Son of God keeps them safe, and the evil one does not get hold of them.

es.L: Sabemos que todo el que ha nacido de Dios no peca, sino que el que nació de Dios lo guarda, y el maligno no lo toca.
es.B: Sabemos que quien ha nacido de Dios no sigue pecando; al contrario, el Hijo, que nació de Dios, lo mantiene a salvo, y el maligno no logra atraparlo.
es.R: Sabemos que los hijos de Dios no siguen pecando. El Hijo de Dios los mantiene a salvo, y el maligno no puede apoderarse de ellos.

fr.L: Nous savons que quiconque est né de Dieu ne pèche pas, mais celui qui a été engendré de Dieu le garde, et le Mauvais ne le touche pas.
fr.B: Nous savons que quiconque est né de Dieu ne continue pas à pécher ; au contraire, le Fils, qui a été engendré de Dieu, le garde, et le Mauvais n’a pas de prise sur lui.
fr.R: Nous savons que les enfants de Dieu ne continuent pas à pécher. Le Fils de Dieu les protège, et le Mauvais ne peut pas s’emparer d’eux.

sw.L: Tunajua kwamba kila aliyezaliwa kutoka kwa Mungu hatendi dhambi, bali yule aliyezaliwa kutoka kwa Mungu anamlinda, na yule mwovu hamgusi.
sw.B: Tunajua kwamba kila aliyezaliwa na Mungu haendelei kutenda dhambi; badala yake, Mwana, aliyezaliwa na Mungu, humlinda salama, na yule mwovu hamshiki.
sw.R: Tunajua kwamba watoto wa Mungu hawaendelei kutenda dhambi. Mwana wa Mungu huwalinda salama, na yule mwovu hawezi kuwakamata.

ko.L: 우리는 하나님에게서 난 사람은 누구나 죄를 짓지 않는다는 것을 압니다. 오히려 하나님에게서 나신 분이 그를 지키시고, 악한 자는 그를 건드리지 못합니다.
ko.B: 우리는 하나님에게서 태어난 사람은 계속 죄를 짓지 않는다는 것을 압니다. 오히려 하나님에게서 나신 아들께서 그를 안전하게 지키시고, 악한 자는 그를 손대지 못합니다.
ko.R: 우리는 하나님의 자녀들이 계속 죄를 짓지 않는다는 것을 압니다. 하나님의 아들께서 그들을 안전하게 지켜 주시고, 악한 자는 그들을 붙잡지 못합니다.

vi.L: Chúng ta biết rằng ai đã được sinh ra từ Đức Chúa Trời thì không phạm tội, nhưng Đấng đã được sinh ra từ Đức Chúa Trời gìn giữ người ấy, và kẻ ác không đụng đến người ấy được.
vi.B: Chúng ta biết rằng ai được sinh ra từ Đức Chúa Trời thì không cứ phạm tội; trái lại, Con, là Đấng được sinh ra từ Đức Chúa Trời, gìn giữ người ấy an toàn, và kẻ ác không nắm giữ được người ấy.
vi.R: Chúng ta biết rằng con cái Đức Chúa Trời không tiếp tục phạm tội. Con Đức Chúa Trời giữ họ an toàn, và kẻ ác không thể nắm lấy họ.

decisions.choice: does not go on sinning: does not live in sin
decisions.reason: The present ἁμαρτάνει describes a settled way of life, as in 3:6 and 3:9. The letter has already said that believers do sin and must confess it (1:8-2:2), and 5:16 has just spoken of a believer who sins.

decisions.choice: the one born of God who keeps is Jesus, the Son; he keeps the believer
decisions.reason: The first participle (γεγεννημένος) is perfect, as everywhere in the letter for believers. The second (γεννηθεὶς) is aorist and appears to mean someone else: the Son, who keeps those the Father gave him (John 17:12). The SBLGNT reads αὐτόν (him), the believer whom the Son keeps. Many manuscripts read the reflexive pronoun (ἑαυτοῦ, as in 5:21: "keeps himself"), so that the believer guards himself, as in 5:21, and that reading is followed by the King James Version. The letter nowhere else calls Jesus "born of God", which is the other side. A footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: him (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, including some early ones, read the reflexive "himself"; others read "him" as the SBLGNT does. The choice goes with meaning decision m2. A reviewer should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the evil one does not touch him: cannot seize or harm him
alternatives: does not come into contact with him at all
decisions.reason: ἅπτεται here means to lay hold of in order to harm. The evil one is the devil (2:13-14; 3:8, 12), who holds the whole world (5:19) but cannot get hold of the one the Son keeps.

decisions.choice: the Son, who was born of God (B); the Son of God (R)
alternatives: the one who was born of God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one meant (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the bare participle.

decisions.choice: God's children ... them
alternatives: everyone who has been born of God ... him
decisions.reason: Readable puts the general singular in the plural, which needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands for any believer, so the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: lo, no gender span
decisions.reason: "Lo" agrees with "todo el que" and "quien", which already cover men and women, so Spanish needs no counterpart to the English span "them|him"; a span here would only make the sentence heavier.

decisions.choice: "est né de Dieu" for the believer; "a été engendré de Dieu" for the Son (L, B)
decisions.reason: The Greek changes the form of the verb for the second participle, which refers to the Son (meaning decision m2). French marks the difference with "engendré", the traditional word for the Son's relation to the Father, so the reader does not take the two as the same person.

decisions.choice: le Mauvais, with a capital (also 5:19)
decisions.reason: The evil one is a person (5:19, meaning decision m2). "Le Mauvais" says plainly that he is evil; "le Malin" is traditional but today mostly means "cunning". The capital marks it as a name.

decisions.choice: yule mwovu
decisions.reason: "The evil one" is a person (as in verse 19, m2), and "yule mwovu" says so while keeping John's title. Naming him "Shetani" would go beyond the wording, and "uovu" (evil) would lose the person.

decisions.choice: "하나님에게서 나신 분" (L) with the honorific; "하나님에게서 나신 아들" (B); "하나님의 아들" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the one born of God who keeps as Jesus, the Son, keeping the believer, and footnotes the reading "keeps himself". Korean marks Jesus with the honorific "나신 분", where the Greek uses a different tense; Balanced and Readable name the Son, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Đấng đã được sinh ra từ Đức Chúa Trời" (L), capitalised
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the one who keeps as Jesus, the Son (m2, uncertain), so Vietnamese writes "Đấng", the word for a divine person; Balanced and Readable name the Son, as the English does.

source.text: οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐσμεν, καὶ ὁ κόσμος ὅλος ἐν τῷ πονηρῷ κεῖται.

records.literal_gloss: We know that from the God we are, and the world whole in the evil [one] lies.

en.L: We know that we are of God, and the whole world lies in the evil one.
en.B: We know that we belong to God, and that the whole world lies in the grip of the evil one.
en.R: We know that we belong to God. But the whole world is held in the power of the evil one.

es.L: Sabemos que somos de Dios, y el mundo entero yace en el maligno.
es.B: Sabemos que pertenecemos a Dios, y que el mundo entero está en las garras del maligno.
es.R: Sabemos que pertenecemos a Dios. Pero el mundo entero está en poder del maligno.

fr.L: Nous savons que nous sommes de Dieu, et le monde entier gît dans le Mauvais.
fr.B: Nous savons que nous appartenons à Dieu, et que le monde entier est sous l’emprise du Mauvais.
fr.R: Nous savons que nous appartenons à Dieu. Mais le monde entier est tenu sous le pouvoir du Mauvais.

sw.L: Tunajua kwamba sisi ni wa Mungu, na ulimwengu wote umelala katika yule mwovu.
sw.B: Tunajua kwamba sisi ni watu wa Mungu, na kwamba ulimwengu wote uko katika makucha ya yule mwovu.
sw.R: Tunajua kwamba sisi ni watu wa Mungu. Lakini ulimwengu wote uko chini ya mamlaka ya yule mwovu.

ko.L: 우리는 우리가 하나님에게서 났고, 온 세상은 악한 자 안에 놓여 있다는 것을 압니다.
ko.B: 우리는 우리가 하나님께 속해 있고, 온 세상은 악한 자의 손아귀에 놓여 있다는 것을 압니다.
ko.R: 우리는 우리가 하나님께 속해 있다는 것을 압니다. 그러나 온 세상은 악한 자의 권세 아래 있습니다.

vi.L: Chúng ta biết rằng chúng ta là từ Đức Chúa Trời, và cả thế gian nằm trong kẻ ác.
vi.B: Chúng ta biết rằng mình thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời, và cả thế gian đang nằm trong tay kẻ ác.
vi.R: Chúng ta biết rằng mình thuộc về Đức Chúa Trời. Nhưng cả thế gian đang ở dưới quyền lực của kẻ ác.

decisions.choice: we are of God: we come from God and belong to him
alternatives: we are God's in origin only
decisions.reason: "Of God" (ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ) in 1 John speaks of where a person comes from and to whom they belong (3:10; 4:4, 6); it echoes being born of God in verse 18.

decisions.choice: the evil one, a person
decisions.reason: The form can be masculine or neuter. Verse 18 has just named "the evil one", so it is the devil here too.

decisions.choice: the world: humanity organized apart from God
decisions.reason: Key term. As in 5:4, the world is not the creation as such but human life set against God.

decisions.choice: lies in the evil one: lies under his power, passive in his hands
decisions.reason: The verb means to lie, to be placed: the world lies passive in the evil one's hold.

decisions.choice: lies in the grip of (B); is held in the power of (R)
decisions.reason: "Lies in the evil one" is unclear in English; Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m4).

source.text: οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἥκει, καὶ δέδωκεν ἡμῖν διάνοιαν ἵνα γινώσκωμεν τὸν ἀληθινόν· καὶ ἐσμὲν ἐν τῷ ἀληθινῷ, ἐν τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ.

records.literal_gloss: We know and that the Son of the God has come, and he has given to us understanding so that we may know the true [one]; and we are in the true [one], in the Son of him Jesus Christ.

en.L: And we know that the Son of God has come, and has given us understanding so that we may know the true one; and we are in the true one, in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: We know too that the Son of God has come and has given us insight to know the one who is true. And we are in the one who is true, since we are in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: We also know that the Son of God has come. He has helped us understand, so that we know the true God. And we are joined to the true God because we are joined to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

es.L: Y sabemos que el Hijo de Dios ha llegado y nos ha dado capacidad de entender, para que conozcamos al verdadero; y estamos en el verdadero, en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: Sabemos también que el Hijo de Dios ha venido y nos ha dado la capacidad de comprender, para que conozcamos a aquel que es verdadero. Y estamos en aquel que es verdadero, ya que estamos en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: También sabemos que el Hijo de Dios ha venido. Nos ha ayudado a entender, para que conozcamos al Dios verdadero. Y estamos unidos al Dios verdadero porque estamos unidos a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.

fr.L: Et nous savons que le Fils de Dieu est venu, et nous a donné l’intelligence afin que nous connaissions celui qui est véritable ; et nous sommes dans celui qui est véritable, dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Nous savons aussi que le Fils de Dieu est venu et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a donné l’intelligence pour connaître celui qui est véritable. Et nous sommes en celui qui est véritable, puisque nous sommes en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Nous savons aussi que le Fils de Dieu est venu. Il nous a aidés à comprendre, pour que nous connaissions le vrai Dieu. Et nous sommes unis au vrai Dieu, parce que nous sommes unis à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.

ko.L: 그리고 우리는 하나님의 아들이 오셔서, 우리에게 참되신 분을 알게 하시려고 깨닫는 마음을 주셨다는 것을 압니다. 그리고 우리는 참되신 분 안에, 곧 그분의 아들 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 안에 있습니다.

ko.R: 우리는 또 하나님의 아들께서 오셨다는 것을 압니다. 그분은 우리가 깨닫게 도와주셔서, 우리가 참하나님을 알게 하셨습니다. 그리고 우리는 참하나님과 하나로 이어져 있습니다. 우리가 그분의 아들 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}와 하나로 이어져 있기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: has come: he came and is now here
decisions.reason: ἥκει is present in form but means "have come and be present".

decisions.choice: the true one: God the Father, the real God
alternatives: the one who tells the truth
decisions.reason: ἀληθινός means real, genuine, as opposed to false gods (verse 21; John 17:3, "the only true God"). The next words, "his Son", show that the true one here is the Father.

decisions.choice: we are in the true one by being in his Son
alternatives: two separate statements: we are in the Father, and we are in the Son
the true one is the Son
decisions.reason: The second "in" phrase explains the first: believers are in God because they are in his Son (2:23-24; John 14:6, 20; 17:21). Because the Son is "his Son", the true one cannot here be the Son himself.

decisions.choice: understanding: the ability to know and grasp
decisions.reason: διάνοιαν is the capacity to understand; the Son gives it so that believers know God himself.

decisions.choice: the true one (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "God" after "the true one". The sense is the same, so no footnote. A reviewer should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the true God
decisions.reason: Readable names the true one (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: since we are in (B); because we are joined to (R)
decisions.reason: The levels make explicit how the two "in" phrases are linked (meaning decision m3). Readable says "joined to" for being "in" someone, which young readers can picture.

decisions.choice: ha llegado
decisions.reason: The verb means he has come and is now here (m1). Literal says "ha llegado", which in Spanish implies arrival and presence; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary "ha venido".

decisions.choice: celui qui est véritable (L, B); le vrai Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: The word means real, genuine, as against false gods (meaning decision m2), which French "véritable" says more clearly than "vrai". A capitalised "le Véritable" would read as a title; the relative clause keeps it a description, as the English "the one who is true" does.

decisions.choice: amefika
decisions.reason: The verb means he has come and is now here (m1). Literal says "amefika" (has arrived), which implies presence; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary "amekuja".

decisions.choice: "참되신 분" (L, B); "참하나님" (R)
decisions.reason: The true one is God the Father, the real God (meaning decision). The adjective is "참" in Korean, as the style guide sets ("참 빛"); "진리" stays for the noun.

decisions.choice: "Đấng chân thật" (L, B) for the true one
decisions.reason: The true one is God the Father, the real God (m2). "Chân thật" keeps the root of "chân lý", so the link with truth in the letter stays; Readable says "the true God", as the Vietnamese John does in 17:3.

decisions.choice: "this one" may be Jesus Christ or God the Father; the text leaves it open
alternatives: Jesus Christ is the true God and eternal life
the Father is the true God and eternal life
decisions.reason: οὗτός can point to the nearest person named, Jesus Christ, or to the main subject, "the true one" of the previous sentence. For Jesus: he is the last person named; the letter calls him "the eternal life" (1:2; compare John 11:25; 14:6); and John's Gospel calls him God (John 1:1, 18; 20:28). For the Father: "the true one" has just been used of him twice; John 17:3 calls the Father "the only true God"; and the sentence would sum up that the God the Son reveals is the real God, against the idols of verse 21. Grammar alone does not decide. Every level keeps the open "this one" and the footnote gives both readings.

decisions.choice: one article over two nouns: one person who is both
decisions.reason: The article stands before "true God" only, and "eternal life" follows without its own: the same one is both the true God and eternal life.

decisions.choice: This one
decisions.reason: "He" could suggest that the subject has been settled; "this one" keeps the Greek pointer, which can refer back to either person (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Este, no span
decisions.reason: "Este" points back without saying whether it is Jesus Christ or the Father, leaving the question open as the Greek does (m1). "Él" would lean toward the nearest name; like the English "This one", the demonstrative takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: Celui-ci, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in English, "Il" or "C’est lui" would point to one person and settle a question the text leaves open (meaning decision m1). The demonstrative can refer back to either the Son or the true one; like the English "this one" it is not a personal pronoun and takes no span.

decisions.choice: Huyu, no span
decisions.reason: "Huyu" (this one) points back without saying whether it is Jesus Christ or the Father, leaving the question open as the Greek does (m1). Like the English "This one", the demonstrative takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "이분" for "this one", with the honorific
decisions.reason: The meaning decision leaves open whether "this one" is Jesus Christ or God the Father, and footnotes it. Korean "이분" points back as openly as the Greek, and the honorific fits either.

decisions.choice: "Đấng ấy" for "this one" at every level
decisions.reason: "This one" may be Jesus Christ or God the Father, and the text leaves it open (m1, uncertain). "Đấng ấy" points back without choosing, as the English "This one" does.

decisions.choice: idols: anything put in the place of the true God, images of false gods included
alternatives: only the images worshiped in pagan temples
decisions.reason: εἴδωλον means an image of a god, and the readers lived among temples and their images. Coming straight after "the true God" (verse 20), the word sets every false god against the real one: pagan worship, and also any false picture of God, such as the teaching about Christ the letter has opposed (2:22-23; 4:1-3). The text does not narrow it.

decisions.choice: little children: a term of affection for the readers
decisions.reason: Τεκνία is the diminutive the writer uses for his readers throughout the letter (2:1, 12, 28; 3:7, 18; 4:4). It is neuter and inclusive, so the gender setting does not apply.

decisions.choice: guard yourselves: a single, decisive command
decisions.reason: The aorist imperative φυλάξατε calls for watchfulness now; the believer's guarding of himself goes with the Son's keeping in verse 18.

decisions.choice: Dear children
decisions.reason: The diminutive expresses affection (meaning decision m2); "little children" can sound as if the readers were small children. Literal keeps the diminutive.

decisions.choice: the false gods people put in the place of the true God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what an idol is and links it to verse 20 (meaning decision m1). It is an explanation of the word, not an application.

decisions.choice: Hijitos (L); Hijitos míos (B); Hijos queridos (R)
decisions.reason: A term of affection (m2), as in John 13:33, where Spanish says "Hijitos". "Hijitos" is warm, not childish; Readable says "Hijos queridos", as the English says "Dear children".

decisions.choice: Watoto wadogo (L); Wanangu wapendwa (B, R)
decisions.reason: A term of affection (m2), as in John 13:33. Balanced and Readable say "my dear children", as the English says "Dear children".

decisions.choice: "사람들이 참하나님 대신에 섬기는 거짓 신들" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads idols as anything put in the place of the true God, images of false gods included, and footnotes it; Readable says what idols are, linking back to "참하나님" in verse 20, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "các thần tượng" for idols
decisions.reason: Idols are anything put in the place of the true God, images of false gods included (m1, uncertain). "Thần tượng" names a false god that is worshipped, while "hình tượng" is the image itself.
